title: Layer-Wise Analysis of Unrolled Inverse Scattering Networks: Boundedness and Non-Contraction
content: Deep-unrolled inverse-scattering networks combine physics-based iterations with learned corrections, yet stability of the trained composite is not implied by solver convergence. We analyse the layers of a Born/contrast-source formulation and turn that gap into a computable test. The layer Jacobian contains an explicit contrast-to-field coupling block, giving a state-dependent sufficient condition for non-contraction: above the threshold αc no correction confined to the contrast channel makes the evaluated layer contractive. Under β₀< 1 the field subsystem contracts, and a nonexpansive contrast projection with a positive damping floor gives the rollout an invariant bounded set; a finite-depth perturbation bound follows without assuming contraction of the composite. The weak-scattering constant β₀ follows from the acquisition operator and the contrast bound, whereas the threshold αc depends on the field state at which the layer is evaluated; both are computable before training for a reference configuration. On synthetic data β₀=0.8303< 1 while the measured spectral norm of the full layer exceeds one; experiments test the bound, the budget constraints, depth and noise. On the published Institut Fresnel geometry the test returns β₀>1, so no a-priori certificate is claimed there, and the measured reconstruction is a finite-depth evaluation with untransferred weights.
